chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Al-Fadala, from Aban, from Al-Zurari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: 'A man prays while sitting and recites the Surah; when he wishes to conclude it, he stands up and bows with the last part of it.' He said: 'His prayer is the prayer of the one who stands.'

key_terms.صَلَاتُ الْقَائِمِ: the prayer of the one who stands

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person who stands up to bow at the end of the Surah while praying sitting?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a worshipper praying while seated who stands up to perform the ruku' (bowing) at the conclusion of the Surah recitation has fulfilled the standing requirement, rendering their prayer equivalent to that of one who remains standing throughout (salat al-qaim). This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the physical postures of prayer, emphasizing the validity of the action over rigid continuity of stance, provided the essential components are performed with due reverence.
